title: Quentin and the Kitchen
author: Bram Coldharbour
blurb: Hazel Underhill, a ghostwriter secretly penning a rival's memoirs, keeps love in the past tense where it belongs. Then the anonymous pen-pal assignment pairs enemies instead of strangers — and they are pulled straight into the middle of it. Now they must say the sentence that has been rehearsed for a decade, and time is already running out.
style: atmospheric and lyrical, with strong sensory detail
